topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the course structure, target audience, and key learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Genetic alterations, differentiation failure, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes cause cancer by disrupting normal cellular differentiation programs and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, and stepwise progression
topics.groupedBecause: They characterize the pathological, histological, and terminological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of invasion, metastasis, and stepwise neoplastic progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity, mortality, and comparative incidence
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause illness and death alongside cancer incidence patterns across human populations and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical challenges of population screening programs for detecting precursor and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the session by summarizing learning expectations and providing reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
